sections.heading: How to Play Fire
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Fire"][color=c8]Fire Mage Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
Fire Mage gameplay is simple with very few skills, but most of the difficulty of Fire comes down to execution. You will often be reacting based on whether one of your spells scores a Critical Strike, which grants [spell=48107]. This can be converted with [spell=108853] into [spell=48108] for instant cast [spell=11366]s. 



[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center]
[table style=grid][tr][td]
	[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=5%][icon name=ability_ironmaidens_grapeshotblast size=medium type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=mage]Convert and Spend Hot Streak:[/color][/b] Critical strikes generate [spell=48107] and [spell=48108], spend these on [spell=11366] (or [spell=2120] in AoE). Use [spell=108853] to convert Heating up into Hot Streak. [/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[hr]
	[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=5%][icon name=spell_fire_sealoffire size=medium type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=mage]Combustion is Key:[/color][/b] [spell=190319] makes all spells guaranteed Critical Strikes, supercharging [spell=48108] generation. This spell can be cast while casting, so try to always activate it at the end of a cast.[/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[hr]
	[table]
	[tr][td width=5%][icon name=spell_fire_fireball size=medium type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=mage]Don't Waste Time:[/color][/b] Sitting on capped [spell=108853] charges, or using them when you already have [spell=48108] up is wasteful. Try to make full use of cooldowns and buffs. [b]Always be casting.[/b][/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c8][icon name=spell_fire_firebolt02 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c8][/icon] Fire Mage Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]
Fire Mage only has one major cooldown ([spell=190319]), but it has a huge impact on gameplay. [spell=153561] is a minor cooldown, and is mostly used in tandem with [spell=190319].




[pad][pad]

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="Combustion" icon=spell_fire_sealoffire]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c8] Combustion [/color][/h3]
All spells Critically Strike during [spell=190319], making you a [spell=48108] machine gun. It has many interactions that either grant other buffs, increase proc chance, speed up cooldown recovery, or boost damage. 



Other key takeaways are:
[ul]

[li][spell=190319] can be cast while casting. Always cast a hard-cast into [spell=190319], but be sure to activate it before the cast completes. Viable spells are:
[ul]
[li][spell=11366] or [spell=2120] (AoE) with a [spell=269650] proc.[/li]
[li][spell=431044] if [b][color=#a4c2f4]Frostfire[/color][/b].[/li]
[li][spell=2948] if [b][color=#f88a56]Sunfury[/color][/b].[/li]
[li][spell=133].[/li]
[/ul]
[/li]


[li]When playing [spell=205026], [spell=190319] should be delayed until the target reaches 90% health (Typically around 18 seconds).[/li]
[li]If not playing [spell=205026], [spell=190319] should still be delayed on the pull (Around 8-10 seconds).
[ul][li]We do this to pre-stack buffs like [spell=1257348] and because [spell=108853] charges are plentiful.[/li][/ul][/li]

[li]In cases where the [spell=205026] window will last longer than 30 seconds, [spell=190319] on the pull and make use of it after.[/li]

[li]After the opener, [spell=190319] should generally be used on cooldown. Sometimes you will delay [spell=190319] for better overlaps with AoE, Damage amps, or to avoid forced downtime.[b] Plan ahead so you don't end up delaying and having it backfire, by costing you a use.[/b][/li]
[li][spell=1257348] is our new Apex talent. It has a chance to proc when you spend [spell=48108].
[ul]
[li][spell=190319] can be extended by [spell=1257348] procs.[/li]
[li]During [spell=190319], your first 3 [spell=1257348] procs are almost guaranteed.[/li]
[/ul]
[/li]

[li][spell=383634] speeds up the [spell=108853] cooldown during [spell=190319].[/li]
[li]Critical Strike is not useless during [spell=190319]. [spell=1254512] and [spell=383967] convert Crit into other effects. Unfortunately, this does not boost Critical Strike much.[/li]
[li]When [spell=190319] ends, [spell=1271177] causes all targets with an active [spell=12846] to take extra damage (if playing the talent). This damage depends on the "size" of the Ignite.
[ul][li]Try to maximize [spell=1271177] in AoE  by having [spell=190319] end while targets are still alive.[/li][/ul][/li]
[/ul]


[hr]




For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-sunfury] [color=#f88a56]Sunfury[/color] the [spell=190319] window is longer, summons an [spell=448659], and ends with [spell=383874]:

[ul][li][spell=383874] is a buff that allows you to rapidly fire [spell=11366] or [spell=2120] casts.[/li]
[li]These casts are free, guaranteed to Crit, and ramp in damage.[/li]
[li]You also gain a Haste buff from [spell=1260272] during this time. [/li]
[/ul]

For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-frostfire] [color=#a4c2f4]Frostfire[/color] the [spell=190319] window is shorter and has no follow-up buffs.  
[/tab]

[/tabs]

sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c8][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c8][/icon] Fire Mage Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]
The best thing you can do to improve your damage as a Fire Mage is to [u]always be casting[/u]. Idle time in combat, caused by inactivity or poor movement, adds up and will greatly affect your damage. Mastering movement and keeping focus during combat is unequivocally the best way to raise your damage.
[pad]

[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="12.1 Tier Set and Pyroclasm" icon=spell_shaman_lavasurge]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c8] Pyroclasm Hardcasts with the 12.1 tier set[/color][/h3]
The 12.1 tier set greatly improves the potency of [spell=269650] making it stronger, faster, and always crit.

[b]With the 12.1 tier bonus[/b], [symbol=wow-hero-talent-sunfury] [color=#f88a56]Sunfury[/color] will generally use [spell=269650] procs as it gets them, even leading up to [spell=190319]. You can always set up [spell=190319] by using [spell=153561] for a [spell=269650] proc (via [spell=449349]) leading to to the cooldown, hard-casting [spell=11366] right as Combustion is available, and activating Combustion right before the cast completes.

[b]With the 12.1 tier bonus[/b], [symbol=wow-hero-talent-frostfire] [color=#a4c2f4]Frostfire[/color] should try to always have at least one [spell=269650] proc banked leading up to [spell=190319]. Hard-cast [spell=11366] right as Combustion is available, and activate Combustion right before the cast completes. [spell=153561] can be used afterwards.

As both versions, [spell=269650] is used more aggressively outside of [spell=190319]. During [spell=190319], procs should be spent once [spell=108853] charges have run dry.



During [spell=190319], check the remaining time before beginning your [spell=11366] hard-casts with [spell=269650]. It is wasteful if the spell completes right after [spell=190319] expires. If you begin a [spell=11366] hard-cast with [spell=269650], always try to complete it. This is true even if it will not finish during [spell=190319]. Do not a interrupt a cast once you have started it. [spell=212653] should be used to move as needed, so try to save this precious resource. 

Avoid securing [spell=48108] with [spell=108853] during [spell=2120] hard-cast with [spell=269650]. There is a bug with [spell=269650] specific to [spell=2120]. A hard-cast [spell=2120] queued into a [spell=48108] [spell=2120] will not return a [spell=48108]. This will result in a munched crit, and should be avoided. If you have [spell=48107], leave it that way. Once the hard-cast finishes, follow up with the instant [spell=2120]. 

[/tab]

[tab name="Double Pyroblast" icon=spell_fire_fireball02]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c8] Double Pyroblast and Finding your Rhythm[/color][/h3]
This guide has many mentions to "Double Pyroblast". When a [spell=133] (or other cast) completes, and is followed by an instant [spell=11366], both spells go off at the same time. If both Critically Strike, you will gain another [spell=48108]. Normally this is hard to predict, but [spell=205026] and [spell=190319] make it guaranteed. This works because two spells were in flight, and two spells Crit. If two spells Crit at the same time, you skip [spell=48107], straight to [spell=48108]. That is Double Pyroblast.

The beauty of Double Pyroblast is that it places the travel time of the spells during Global Cooldown, meaning that you won't lost time waiting for them to hit. There are many ways you can pull this off, but the key factors are:

[ul][li]You are guaranteed to Crit.[/li]
[li]You are currently casting a spell that can generate [spell=48108] ([spell=133], [spell=2948], etc.).[/li]
[li]You have [spell=48108] in hand [i]before[/i] the cast completes.[/li]
[li]You queue a [spell=48108] spender ([spell=11366] or [spell=2120]) [i]as[/i] the cast completes.[/li]
[/ul]
Be warned, a [spell=2120] hard-cast queued into a [spell=48108] [spell=2120] will not work due to a long-standing bug.

So to reiterate on the most basic example: Begin casting [spell=133], convert [spell=48107] into [spell=48108] with [spell=108853] while casting (try doing it midway through the cast), then press [spell=11366] as the [spell=133] finishes. If both Crit, press [spell=11366] again. If this is still not working for you, know that you are not alone. It's so common that we have devised a training method for you:
[toggler name="Double Pyroblast Exercise" closed=true toc=false size=6]

[pad]
The timing of your spellcasts and travel-times as a Fire Mage is something you should familiarize yourself with, and the best way to understand Double Pyroblast is to see it yourself. Practicing Double Pyroblast achieves both goals! Find a Target Dummy that is above 90% health, spec Sunfury with [spell=205026], unequip your gear, and repeat the following sequence:

Pre-cast [spell=11366] (Do not repeat this step).
[ol][li][spell=133][/li]
[li][spell=108853] (if available) or [spell=133][/li]
[li]Queue [spell=11366] as the [spell=133] ends.[/li]
[li][spell=11366] again.[/li]
[li][i]Repeat from Step 1.[/i][/li][/ol]

The goal is to get to the point where you can repeat this sequence indefinitely, without mistakes. Add pieces of loot back one by one to bring your Haste back to normal levels. You can also cast [spell=80353] to increase the pace. Once you feel comfortable, you only need to add [spell=190319] (Between Step 2 and 3) and you have it down! 

[/toggler]

[tab name="Emergency Shimmer" icon=spell_mage_altertime]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c8] Alter Time + Time Walk = Bonus Shimmer[/color][/h3]
With the [spell=1244087] talent, [spell=342245] can be used as a way to secure a [spell=212653] in case of emergency. Simply double-tap your [spell=342245] to activate it and instantly return, then [spell=212653]. So long as you have the [spell=1244087] talent, you will always have a charge doing this. 

This is not the most effective use of [spell=342245], but sometimes a [spell=212653] can be the difference between life and death.

[pad]

Our Fire Mage guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Fire Mage guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].





[tooltip name=GI][color=q]Bank 1 [spell=108853] for [spell=449394], but make sure to use them all before [spell=190319] ends.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=ScorchHaste][color=q]If you are above 104% haste, don't attempt to get [spell=48108]. 

Cast [spell=133] instead of [spell=2948] if you already have a  [spell=48108].

[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=firedup][color=q]Prioritize spending all [spell=108853] charges in [spell=190319] over spending [spell=269650]. 

Ideally, make sure the cast time of [spell=11366] is shorter than the remaining duration of [spell=190319]. 

If you notice mid-cast that [spell=190319] will end before the cast completes, do not interrupt the spell. [u]Commit to it.[/u] The damage loss of interrupting the cast is far greater than misjudging the timing. 
[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=pool][color=q]Stop using [spell=108853] charges and [spell=269650] buffs if [spell=190319] will be up soon to ensure they are available during cooldowns.

[tooltip name=sfbust][color=q]If [spell=190319] is ready, hard-cast a spell and activate [spell=190319] right before the cast completes. Priority of spells to hard-cast:

[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=ffbust][color=q]If [spell=190319] is ready, hard-cast a spell and activate [spell=190319] right before the cast completes. Priority of spells to hard-cast:

[tooltip name=fsbug][color=q]Two simultaneous [spell=2120] casts (one hard-cast, one instant with [spell=48108]) will "munch" the proc and not result in a [spell=48108].

[tooltip name=whiffmeat][color=q]The goal here is to proc [spell=269650] before the pull without entering combat.

[tooltip name=lastms][color=q]You must activate [spell=190319] in the last 150 milliseconds of the [spell=11366] cast for this opener. 

Distance to the target is also a concern, avoid long travel times.

[tooltip name=dblpyro][color=q]If [spell=133] and the instant [spell=11366] leave your hands at the same time, both crit. This means you get [spell=48108] for another [spell=11366]. [/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=execute][color=q]Execute refers to <=30% health. This is the range where [spell=450746] becomes active.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=ib1][color=q]Above 90% ([spell=205026]), [spell=133] and [spell=11366] will always Critically Strike. This means you can anticipate [spell=48107]. 

If you just cast [spell=11366] (without [spell=133]), and only one spell is in flight, you can alternate between [spell=108853] and [spell=11366].

Do this until you run out of [spell=108853], or the target reaches 90% health.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=ib2][color=q][spell=11366] is instant and will always Critically Strike during [spell=383860]. [/color][/tooltip]

Flip the logic and use [spell=108853] to generate [spell=48107] while casting [spell=2948]. Follow up with [spell=11366] (since [spell=2948] is guaranteed to Crit).[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=ib4][color=q]In execute, try and play close to the target so you can react quickly when your [spell=11366]s Crit. Converting these [spell=48107] to [spell=48108] before beginning a [spell=2948] makes you waste less Crits.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=ib5][color=q]During filler, secure the [spell=48108] and queue your instant [spell=11366] as a [spell=133] ends. If two spells hit at the same time, there is a grace period for counting crits.[/color][/tooltip]
